description: Automatic affected C# tests and live, retained code coverage for .NET 10+ and Microsoft.Testing.Platform.
command.refreshTests: Rebuild and Run All C# Tests
command.runFile: Run Affected Tests for This File
command.runFolder: Run Affected Tests for This Folder or Project
command.showSlowestTests: Show Slowest Test Files and Tests
command.debugCoveringTests: Debug a Test Covering This Line
config.autoRun: Automatically run affected tests after changes. The first time a workspace opens, Testy asks before building and running the baseline. Pausing from the status bar or Test Explorer is remembered per workspace without changing this setting.
config.runMode: Choose affected test files or the entire C# suite.
config.runMode.affected: Use recorded code usage, with project fallback when information is incomplete.
config.runMode.all: Run every C# test file after a change.
config.selectionGranularity: How closely `affected` mode matches an edit to the tests it can affect.
config.selectionGranularity.method: Run the test files whose coverage reached an edited method, accessor or constructor body.
config.selectionGranularity.file: Run every test file whose coverage reached the edited file. Choose this when tests depend on the source line numbers of code they did not change, for example through `[CallerLineNumber]`.
config.selectionGranularity.test: Run only the tests whose own coverage executed an edited body. Each test file's tests then run one at a time in its test process, so Testy learns every test's coverage; this costs a collector snapshot per test. Tests that depend on state an earlier test in the same process initialized (a cached value, a lazily created singleton) can be missed: use `#testy.safetyNet#` to run the rest in the background.
config.safetyNet: After an automatic `affected` run, run the test files it did not select once the editor has been quiet for two seconds. Any change cancels them until the next quiet period, so they never delay feedback on a save. A file that fails although its latest results passed is reported in Output, since the change that broke it was not selected.
config.safetyNet.off: Run only the selected test files.
config.safetyNet.related: Also run the other test files of the test projects the changes affect.
config.safetyNet.all: Also run every other test file.
config.excludeTraits: Test traits that automatic runs leave out, for example `Integration` or `Category=Slow`. `Key=Value` matches that trait; a bare value matches an MSTest `TestCategory`, NUnit `Category` or xUnit `Category` trait of that value. Matching ignores case. Excluded tests stay in Test Explorer and run when you run them yourself; changes covered only by them select nothing.
config.trigger: Choose which changes trigger automatic tests.
config.trigger.save: Editor saves, plus files renamed or deleted through VS Code.
config.trigger.fileSystem: All matching disk changes, including external edits and branch switches.
config.debounceTime: Milliseconds to wait after the latest change before rebuilding and testing. Unless this is set, `fileSystem` triggers wait 500 ms, since one operation such as a branch switch writes many files; a later change always restarts the wait and cancels an automatic run in progress.
config.runWithCoverage: Collect and retain code coverage. Disabling coverage uses conservative project selection.
config.showCoverage: Also show covered, uncovered and stale markers in editor gutters. Coverage is always available in Test Explorer's coverage view; these markers additionally show **stale** coverage while affected tests rerun. While `#testy.inlineResults#` draws gutter markers, covered lines show its pass/fail marker instead of the covered marker.
config.inlineResults: Inline results for covered lines of C# files, from the test files whose retained coverage hits each line: a green check when they all passed, a red cross when one failed, a grey dash when one has not run since a change (or the file has unsaved edits). While these markers are on, `#testy.showCoverage#` marks only uncovered and stale lines, so each line has one marker. **Clear Coverage** hides both until the next run.
config.inlineResults.gutterAndHover: Pass/fail markers in the gutter, and a hover listing the covering test files with links to run them or show them in Test Explorer.
config.problems.publishBuildDiagnostics: Whether Testy publishes the build errors and warnings of its builds to the Problems panel.
Publish them unless the C# extension is active; it reports the same errors.
Always publish them, even if they can appear twice.
Never publish them; build errors stay in the Testy output and on the failing projects in Test Explorer.
config.solution: Optional `.sln`, `.slnx` or `.slnf` file whose projects limit the test and build entry points. Relative paths resolve against the workspace folder that sets the value (the first folder for workspace-level values); `${workspaceFolder}` is supported. In a multi-root workspace a folder-level value limits only that folder's projects. Leave empty to use every project in the workspace.
config.projects.include: Glob patterns for entry-point projects to include, for example `tests/**/*.csproj`. Empty includes every project. In a multi-root workspace a folder-level value applies only to that folder's projects.
config.projects.exclude: Glob patterns for entry-point projects to exclude. Exclusions win over inclusions. Folder-level patterns add to the workspace patterns and apply only to that folder.
config.fileWatcherPattern: Files whose changes can trigger tests.
config.exclude: Additional glob patterns to ignore. Generated files, `bin`, `obj`, `TestResults`, `node_modules` and `.git` are always excluded. Folder-level patterns add to the workspace patterns and apply only to that folder.
config.buildConfiguration: MSBuild configuration used for builds and test discovery. One value applies to every workspace folder; Testy warns when folder-level values differ and uses the workspace value.
config.additionalConfigurations: Extra MSBuild configurations, for example `Release`. Each adds `Run (Release)`, `Run with coverage (Release)` and `Debug (Release)` profiles to Test Explorer that build, discover and run (or debug) the selected tests with that configuration. Automatic runs always use `#testy.buildConfiguration#`.
config.maxParallelProjects: Worker limit for initial project preparation, builds, source analysis and discovery. `0` automatically uses up to four workers while reserving one CPU; `1` runs sequentially. Applies on the next run.
config.maxParallelTestFiles: Worker limit for test-file execution and private runner preparation. Project-wide batches each use one worker. `0` uses available CPUs minus one, with at least one worker; `1` runs sequentially. Tests sharing external resources may need `1`, or `#testy.exclusiveTraits#` to keep only those files apart. Applies on the next run.
config.exclusiveTraits: Test traits that name a shared external resource, such as a database or a fixed port, for example `Database` or `Resource=Ports`. Two test files with tests matching the same entry never run at the same time; other files still run in parallel. Patterns match like `#testy.excludeTraits#`. A file runs in one test process, so a trait on one of its tests applies to the whole file. Applies on the next run.
config.serialTraits: Test traits whose test files run with no other test file at the same time, for example `Category=Serial`. Patterns match like `#testy.excludeTraits#`. Applies on the next run.
config.reuseTestHosts: Run the test files of each test project in one long-lived test process per worker instead of starting a process per file, and split coverage between them with collector snapshots. Saves the test host's start-up for every file after the first (on by default; a baseline of 120 files took about a third less time). Tests then share static state, loaded assemblies and files in the test output with earlier files of the same process: list traits in `#testy.isolatedTraits#` for test files that need a process of their own, or turn this off for suites that need a fresh process per file. Debug runs always start a new process.
config.testArguments: Additional Microsoft.Testing.Platform application arguments. Discovery, filtering and connection arguments are managed by Testy. One value applies to every workspace folder; Testy warns when folder-level values differ and uses the workspace value.
config.timeoutSeconds: Maximum duration for an individual build, discovery or test-file run. Debug runs are not limited.
config.coverageToolPath: Optional absolute path to `dotnet-coverage`. By default, Testy installs a pinned collector into its own storage on first use.
config.debugConfiguration: Extra properties merged into the `coreclr` attach configuration that Testy's Debug profiles use, for example `{ "justMyCode": false }`. `type` may be overridden; `request` and `processId` are always set by Testy.
config.debugConfiguration.type: Debugger type. Testy uses `coreclr` unless you override it.
config.debugConfiguration.justMyCode: Debug only user code; set to `false` to step into framework and library code.
config.debugConfiguration.requireExactSo: Require source files to match the build exactly.
config.debugConfiguration.suppressJITOpt: Disable JIT optimizations of loaded modules for a better debugging experience in Release builds.
config.debugConfiguration.sourceFileMap: Map build-time source paths to local paths, for example `{ "/src": "${workspaceFolder}" }`.
config.debugConfiguration.symbolOptions: Where the debugger looks for symbol (`.pdb`) files.
Additional directories or symbol server URLs to search.
config.debugConfiguration.sourceLinkOpti: Source Link settings per URL, for example `{ "*": { "enabled": true } }`.
config.debugConfiguration.logging: Debugger logging options, for example `{ "moduleLoad": false }`.
config.debugConfiguration.processId: Always the test host Testy started; Testy sets it.
walkthrough.title: Get started with Testy
walkthrough.description: Run affected C# tests automatically, with retained coverage.
walkthrough.prerequisites.title: Install the prerequisites
walkthrough.prerequisites.description:
Testy needs the .NET 10 SDK or later and C# test projects that use Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP). The C# extension is only needed for debugging tests.
[Download .NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download)
walkthrough.trust.title: Trust the workspace
walkthrough.trust.description:
Testy builds and runs workspace code, so in Restricted Mode it waits and starts as soon as you trust the workspace.
[Manage Workspace Trust](command:workbench.trust.manage)
walkthrough.baseline.title: Let the first baseline finish
walkthrough.baseline.description:
The first time a workspace opens, Testy asks before it builds, discovers and runs every C# test file once to learn which code each test file exercises. Saving a file or running tests also starts it. Follow progress in the status bar.
[Show Output](command:testy.showOutput)
walkthrough.coverage.title: Review coverage
walkthrough.coverage.description:
On first use Testy downloads a pinned Microsoft dotnet-coverage collector from NuGet into its own storage. Coverage appears in Test Explorer's coverage view; gutter markers are optional.
[Open Coverage Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22testy.showCoverage%22%5D)
walkthrough.pause.title: Pause, resume and debug
walkthrough.pause.description:
Save a file to run the affected tests. Pause automatic testing from the status bar or Test Explorer, and debug tests with the Debug profile (requires the C# extension).
[Show Testy Actions](command:testy.showMenu)
capabilities.untrusted: Testy builds and executes workspace code, so in Restricted Mode it waits until the workspace is trusted.
capabilities.virtual: Testy requires the .NET CLI and local workspace files.
viewsWelcome.noTestProjects:
Testy found no C# test project it can run. Testy needs .NET 10 or later test projects that use Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP).
[Show Output](command:testy.showOutput)
[Get Started with Testy](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%22reginaldFerland.testy%23testy.gettingStarted%22)
config.processPriority: Priority of the builds, coverage instrumentation and test processes Testy starts. `belowNormal` keeps the editor responsive while a run uses every CPU; `normal` gives tests the same share of the CPU as other programs, for timing-sensitive tests. Applies to processes started after the change.
config.processPriority.belowNormal: Start Testy's processes below normal priority (default).
config.processPriority.normal: Start Testy's processes at normal priority.
config.finishRunningTests: When a change arrives while an automatic run is testing, test files already running keep running for up to this many seconds to finish and report their results, while no further files start; the next run then starts with the change. When the change affects every running file, the run stops at once; a finished file whose sources the change edited does not keep its coverage. `0` cancels the run at once, as for any other change.
config.testTimeoutSeconds: Limit for each test, in seconds, counted from when the test framework reports the test as started. A test that runs longer stops its test process; it and the tests of its batch that did not finish are reported as errored with the reason. `0` turns the limit off. Frameworks that do not report started tests are limited only by `#testy.timeoutSeconds#`. Debug runs are not limited.
config.splitLongTestFiles: In a baseline, a run of every test and `#testy.runMode#` `all`, split a test file that would otherwise finish alone at the end into parts that several workers run at the same time, by the learned duration of each test. The file's results and coverage are combined as one run. Each part starts its own test process, so the tests of one file can run in different processes; turn this off for test classes whose tests depend on running in one process.
config.isolatedTraits: Traits whose test files always run in a test process of their own, even with `#testy.reuseTestHosts#`, such as `Isolated` or `Category=StaticState`. Use it for tests that change static state, the environment or files in the test output. Matches traits like `#testy.excludeTraits#`; a trait on one test applies to its whole file.
config.testProcessMemoryLimit: With `#testy.reuseTestHosts#`, the memory in MiB a reused test process (with its coverage collector) may use after a test file; a process over it is replaced by a new one for the next file. `0` sets no limit.
config.alwaysRunFailing: Automatic runs also run every test file whose latest results include a failure, whatever changed, until it passes. Pinned tests (**Pin to Automatic Runs** in Test Explorer) always run with automatic runs too.
config.inclusiveTraits: Traits that name a shared external resource test files may use at the same time, such as a database they only read: `Database` or `Resource=Ports`. Files with tests matching the same entry run side by side, but never at the same time as files whose tests match that entry in `#testy.exclusiveTraits#`.
config.workerTraits: Traits whose test files use several CPUs themselves, and how many test-file workers such a file takes while it runs, for example `{ "Category=Parallel": 4 }`. Fewer other files run beside it. A file needs at most `#testy.maxParallelTestFiles#` workers.
